A manually asserted semantic-invariance flag is too weak unless its causal/dependency closure is itself bound and falsifiable.

external_patterns.use: Concept distillation only. Bazel remote caching models an action through declared inputs, command, environment and outputs; hermeticity requires actions to depend only on declared inputs. This supports boundary-input hashing rather than repository-wide churn invalidation.

Use the separation between artifact subject, build definition/parameters and resolved dependencies as a provenance model. This helps bind WHAT was produced and from WHICH known inputs, but does not prove semantic equivalence to a later F2 generation.

decision_rule: At probe binding, freeze exact subject provenance and compute the boundary fingerprint from a declared verified closure.
At promotion/reentry, recompute the same boundary manifest against the candidate current generation.
If closure completeness is UNKNOWN, classify invariance UNKNOWN and fail closed.

If any bound input/config/toolchain/harness identity changes, historical probe remains historical for current promotion unless a new discriminator proves the changed dimension irrelevant at the claimed scope.

If the complete bound closure is byte-identical and artifact/runtime constraints remain compatible, a RUNTIME_SUBJECT_INVARIANT receipt may say that unrelated repository churn did not invalidate this exact boundary. It still does not upgrade the probe beyond its observed runtime tier.
Do not use dynamic coverage/trace membership as authority for closure completeness; it may be diagnostic only because dormant branches and config-dependent imports can be missed.

counterhypotheses.claim: Whole repository SHA equality should remain the only currentness criterion.
counterhypotheses.reason: It prevents false currentness but converts unrelated commits into replay debt and does not exploit exact causal-boundary identity. Keep exact commit as provenance, not necessarily as the sole equivalence predicate.

counterhypotheses.claim: Existing GitHub Actions paths filters already define the needed dependency closure.
counterhypotheses.reason: persistent_agency_kernel.py directly imports multiple production modules absent from the workflow paths list. Path filters are scheduling triggers, not automatically complete semantic dependency manifests.

counterhypotheses.claim: Artifact digest or SLSA/in-toto provenance is sufficient to carry runtime credit forward to newer source.
counterhypotheses.reason: It authenticates the historical subject/build inputs, not semantic equivalence to a successor generation.

counterhypotheses.claim: Dynamic execution coverage can discover the exact relevant closure automatically.
counterhypotheses.reason: Observed coverage can omit dormant/config/error paths; absence from one run is not proof of irrelevance.

mandatory_falsifiers_before_E5: TRANSITIVE_OMISSION: mutate one direct/transitive dependency intentionally omitted from a candidate manifest and show the closure validator rejects UNKNOWN/INCOMPLETE rather than preserving invariance.
UNRELATED_CHURN: mutate an unrelated repository file and show the boundary digest remains unchanged while exact repository provenance records the newer commit.
CONFIG_DRIFT: alter a bound config/schema/environment dimension that changes behavior and prove digest/currentness invalidates.
HARNESS_DRIFT: alter probe command/test harness semantics and prove the probe identity invalidates.
DYNAMIC_IMPORT_UNKNOWN: introduce a runtime-resolved dependency outside statically verified closure and prove fail-closed UNKNOWN unless explicitly materialized into the manifest.
NO_CREDIT_INFLATION: equal boundary fingerprints plus a historical green receipt must not create a higher runtime tier or whole-system PASS.
